children: China's humanoid shipment volumes are likely to remain modest in the near term despite strong growth from a low base, according to Morgan Stanley in a research note. MS estimates China humanoid shipments of 50,000 units in 2026, 100,000 in 2027, and 446,000 by 2030, driven by driven by integrators' efforts to scale deployments. MS notes several risks to further adoption of humanoid robots, including product reliability. "We expect some pilot projects for specific tasks to gradually convert into broader deployments starting in 2027, although the pace of scaling remains uncertain," the bank says. Potential use cases include material handling, logistics sorting and unmanned retail, the bank says. Commercialization will take time to materialize, the bank adds. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
